title: Classic French Toast (Pain Perdu)
description: Classic French Toast (Pain Perdu) is a timeless French breakfast made by soaking thick slices of brioche or challah in a rich vanilla custard before pan-frying to golden perfection. Crisp on the outside and soft, custardy within, it is elegantly finished with powdered sugar, maple syrup, and seasonal berries.

ingredients.title: For the Custard Base
items: 4 slices of brioche or challah (day-old, 1-inch thick)
¼ tsp ground cinnamon (optional, for warmth)
A pinch of fine sea salt

instruction.title: 1. Prepare the Custard
steps: In a mixing bowl, whisk together eggs, cream, milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt until smooth and slightly frothy.
Chef's Tip: Strain the mixture through a fine sieve for an extra-silky custard.

instruction.title: 2. Soak the Bread
steps: Pour the custard into a shallow dish. Lay the brioche slices in it and let them soak for 20–30 seconds per side, just until the bread is saturated but not falling apart.
Professional Trick: Day-old bread holds shape better and absorbs custard more evenly.

instruction.title: 3. Preheat the Pan
steps: Heat a large non-stick skillet or griddle over medium-low heat. Add butter and oil — the oil prevents the butter from burning.

instruction.title: 4. Cook to Golden Perfection
steps: Place the soaked bread slices onto the pan. Cook for 2–3 minutes per side, or until deep golden brown and slightly crisp on the outside.

instruction.title: 5. Finish in the Oven (Optional, Restaurant Method)
steps: Transfer the toast to a 180°C (350°F) oven for 3–5 minutes to ensure the interior is warm and custardy.

instruction.title: 6. Plate Elegantly
steps: Stack two slices on a pre-warmed plate. Dust lightly with powdered sugar, drizzle with warm maple syrup, and garnish with berries and mint. Add a quenelle of whipped cream or crème fraîche on the side.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestion
items: Espresso or cappuccino on the side for a full Continental brunch experience.

chefTips: Add a splash of Grand Marnier, Cointreau, or dark rum to the custard for a French bistro twist.
Infuse the milk with a split vanilla bean or orange zest before whisking.
Texture Tip: The perfect French toast is crisp outside, custardy inside, never soggy.
